body:
Generated starter READMEs used bare `mori` commands, which could select the Node beta executable instead of the Rust CLI that created the Core/1 project. Initialization now writes the creating Rust executable's absolute path, quoted as one POSIX shell word, and identifies the source and local semantics profiles. The path is resolved before reserving the project directory.

The new regression copies the real Rust binary into a path containing spaces, an apostrophe and Unicode, initializes both templates outside the repository, and runs each generated check/simulate/test sequence with an empty PATH. It resolves the host shell before clearing the child's PATH and checks complete financial poststates and ordered effects. Two independent financial expectation packets were frozen before execution.

Validation reproduced the original failure (`mori: not found`, child exit127, one failed test), then passed the complete init target: **8 passed, 0 failed, 0 filtered**, in **54.277505 seconds** including the cold build. Tested source: `3827270579a68df23330a360b5c5b8372e63bab3`, tree `44da41db47de27543b4f3e9f919febdd7ad0ec78`. Both fresh source audits approve the current candidate; both fresh actual-result audits approve the scoped result. Root verified all selected production, dependency, test and existing fixture bytes against current main `588d811dbbd9e88d22d3ebe90b0544672870caa0`; only an unrelated guideline paragraph differs among the 438 checked files. Separate backend/Core2 tests and new immutable fixtures do not alter this consumer. The prepared integration tree is `3a7659529f84444c5e2e7cb9734547b39b727b18`, distinct from the observed test tree. Original RED and superseded source reviews remain preserved.

Observed execution is Linux/POSIX only. Control/backtick presentation and non-UTF-8 path coverage recommendations remain advisory limitations under the designated security review. This is ordinary local tooling; no SDK, proof, key or ledger operation is covered.
title: Keep generated starter commands on the creating Rust CLI
